samples.summary: Board wheel listener bound to `canvas` rather than the container, diverging from production for the exact reason production documents

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out exactly. The hunt harness's board mount (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:537-545) passes only canvas/overlay/store/hostWidth/hostHeight/dpr/viewport to S.initializeEditor — no getSnapGrid. The gridSnap state (page.tsx:401) is consumed solely as a controlled prop on BoardToolbarLazy (page.tsx:746-753); nothing in the mount effect reads it. Meanwhile the shipped charter asserts as measured fact that the toolbar grid snap is switchable and that "Both move a drag away from where you aimed" (scripts/agent/charters-ui/board-author.md:79-83) and "THE GRID CONTROLS ARE REAL … their round trip is worth predicting" (:94-95), and page.tsx:736-742 calls them "REQUIRED and fully controlled". No guard makes this unreachable (?surface=board mounts it), and it is a design-fit/spec-fidelity violation in kind — the harness contradicts its own brief and diverges from production in the direction mem-board-store.ts explicitly warns against — so it is major, not taste.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I found no counterexample. The harness board mount at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:537-545 calls S.initializeEditor without suppressSlideChrome; no indirect path supplies it (index.ts:204 re-exports initialize, and editor.ts:6743 sets no default). Production does pass it (board-view.tsx:288). Without the flag, editor.ts:3421-3443 keeps the slide-scoped "Change layout…" item whose onPick calls store.applyLayout, and keyboard.ts:383/529/556 leave Cmd+D/Cmd+M/Cmd+Shift+D pointed at duplicateSlide/addSlide; the harness store faithfully throws for all of these (mem-board-store.ts:26-61, 74-89). Nothing downstream absorbs the resulting uncaught error: hunt-ui-oracles.mjs:142-151 buffers every pageerror with no allow-list, and hunt-ui-probe.mjs:67 permits right-click. The board charter line "a refusal there is not a finding" (charters-ui/board-author.md:84-87) binds the persona only, and the same charter treats a fired oracle as a finding path (lines 116-117), so it is not a guard. Under the design-fit lens this is a genuine fidelity/fit violation: the harness mount does not mirror the product mount it exists to reproduce, contradicting the harness's own stated rule at mem-board-store.ts:9-13, and it manufactures crash candidates unreachable in production.

verdict.reason: The binding difference exists (harness/hunt/page.tsx:571 binds wheel to `canvas`; board-view.tsx:587-610 binds to `container`), but the failure mode the finding rests on cannot occur in the harness. Production's rationale holds only because BoardView injects `[data-handle] { pointer-events: auto !important; }` into document.head (board-view.tsx:250-252). The hunt harness never mounts BoardView (no `board-view|BoardView` reference anywhere under app/harness; it builds the editor directly at page.tsx:537 and imports only `@/app/board/board-wheel` at page.tsx:487), no CSS file in the repo carries a `[data-handle]` pointer-events rule, and `makeHandle`/`styleHandleInteraction` (slides/src/view/editor/overlay.ts:1027-1047, 492-496) set no pointer-events, so handles inherit `pointer-events: none` from the harness overlay (page.tsx:532). The repo itself documents this dependency (board-view.tsx:247-249; editor.ts:2715-2723: "only handle children with `pointer-events: auto` are caught by the overlay listener"). Therefore a wheel over a handle in the harness hit-tests through to the canvas and the canvas-bound listener does fire; `board.handleCenter`/`board.pointAt` "scroll toward it" advice is honoured, and verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:847-862 exercises that path. The `offsetX/offsetY` vs `clientX - canvasRect.left` point is equivalent for a canvas-bound listener. What remains is an event-plumbing detail (correctness lens) / a "mirror production" preference — minor, not blocking under the design-fit rubric.

verdict.reason:
I looked for any board-side equivalent of the slides targeting/drag proofs and found none.

Facts established:
- `verify-hunt-oracles.mjs` contains exactly one board-specific check, `checkBoardViewport` (lines 825-875), and it asserts only: `board.elements` answers at rest, `board.pointAt(700,1200)` refuses off-screen, a wheel pans the viewport, the same point then resolves, and `board.elements` is byte-identical after the scroll. No click-selects-what-it-names assertion, no drag, no resize, no numeric world→screen mapping assertion.
- The runner block (lines 1717-1786) invokes `checkCellTargeting`, `checkReaderRegistry`, `checkOffscreenRefusal`, `checkBoardViewport`, `checkSlidesTargeting`, `checkSheetToolbar`, `checkControlInventory`, `checkRunColor`, `checkUndoCapability`, `checkSeededFault`, `checkPredictionFunnel`, `checkSlidesDrag`, `checkSeededFaultInServeMode` — nothing board-related besides the viewport check. A repo-wide grep for "board" in that file returns no other board usage.
- The reviewer's sub-claim about `checkReaderRegistry` holds: at lines 357-360 the board branch clicks `board.elementCenter("card")` purely to make handles exist and never reads `board.selection` afterwards; the only `board.selection` expectation (line 312) is the vacuous `Array.isArray(v)`.
- Repo-wide searches found no counterexample anywhere else: `surface=board` is mounted only at verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:827; the only files that reference `board.pointAt`/`board.elementCenter`/`board.handleCenter`/`board.selection` at all are the bridge (implementation), page.tsx (seed), hunt-ui-tool.mjs (reader catalogue), the charter, docs, and this verifier. The charter's measured constants ("700, 420", "520, 380", board-author.md:76-77) appear nowhere else in the tree, so no test or lane pins them. There is a `slides-seed.test.ts` pinning "no element's centre under another" for slides (via `SEED_FRAMES`/`coveredCentres` in slides-seed.ts) with no board analogue — `seedBoardElements` lives only in page.tsx and has no geometry test.
- Board readers are separately implemented in bridge.ts (lines 501-618), not shared with the slides readers, so `checkSlidesTargeting`/`checkSlidesDrag` cannot cover the board's world→screen path even though board-view.tsx reuses the `@wafflebase/slides` editor for the gesture itself.

So the absence is real. I mark confidence low only on the blocking classification: the originating issue's acceptance criteria were not supplied to me, so I could not tie the gap to a named criterion, and "missing verification of a stated measured fact" sits close to the test-adequacy lane. The factual claim itself I could not refute.
